language.script_notes: Uses æ, ø and å; ø and æ are shared only with Norwegian. Street names typically end in -vej or -gade, and also -plads, -torv, -allé, -stræde or -bakke.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White posts with a yellow section on the front face that is absent on the back; they are very abundant, standing along almost every road.
road_furniture.line_paint: All-white markings; major roads often have short-dashed outer edge lines, which is distinctive among the northern neighbours.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: White direction signs with red lettering, often with a metal border; town signs are black on white with a small village illustration; warning triangles have a red border on white, and give-way signs have no outline outside the red border. Sign posts are often rounded tubes. Large utility poles dominate.

architecture.distinctive_building_types: Narrow flagpoles in yards, and locally made Allux mailboxes with rounded lids found nationwide.

nature.vegetation: Farmland and fields with small woods, along a long coast.
nature.terrain: Flat to gently rolling with no mountains; the whole country stays under about 200m.

vehicles.plate_color: White with black text on private cars, with an optional blue EU strip carrying 'DK'; commercial vehicles use yellow plates.
vehicles.plate_format: Two letters followed by five digits (e.g. 'AB 12 345'); no regional meaning.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Yellow-plated vans and taxis; some mixed-use vehicles carry yellow-and-white plates.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Gen 2, 3 and 4, captured from white camera cars.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat southern farmland, similar language family and plates with letters and digits
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Uses æ and ø rather than ä and ö, streets end in -vej or -gade rather than -vägen or -gatan; plates are two letters plus five digits versus three letters plus three digits.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Ø/ø and æ letters, similar language
confusion_set.tiebreaker: All-white road lines with no yellow centre line and flat terrain versus mountains; streets end in -vej rather than -veien or -gata.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat land, brick houses, extensive cycling
confusion_set.tiebreaker: White plates (yellow only for commercial) versus yellow plates for everyone; æ, ø and å appear on signs, and bollards have a yellow front face.
